# Who we are

Sambhavam center is based in Whitefield, Bangalore in the same premises as Orange international preschool, AECS Layout. 

We support children who are neurodiverse and who find it difficult to fit in a classroom or learn from a group. We support children who need extra support in the classroom, and work on the language and communication, social adaptive skills and emotional regulation. 

The central purpose of our work is to empower the families of neurodiverse individuals to identify their needs and support them effectively in the long term. In the short term, we are focused on making our autistic children exercise their agency through the communication means they choose and to learn essential skills to navigate their family and other social spaces, to be internally motivated to continue to engage with learning and excited about new things that come their way.

When we work with neurodiverse children, we bring in our learnings from our collective education and our experiences. We approach the therapy environment as an open space for the children to explore, to understand their inclinations and temperaments in the most objective way possible. We work closely with families to imbibe the child’s current knowledge and context in their learnings. We bring in the theories of learning, child development and education, child psychology together to develop multifaceted understanding on the strengths and challenges the children may be facing. The therapists are provided an environment that stimulates constant learning in the form of program reviews and monthly training. We firmly believe that education and therapy should come together for the children. 

# What we are working towards

We take time to understand the child’s communication, interests, strengths and support needs. We ask how a goal will help the child in everyday life, not only whether it can be achieved during a session. We support children to take part while attending to their choices, communication and need for support. We prepare, document, review and follow through, while adapting when something is not working. We consider what adults and environments can change, rather than placing every demand for change on the child.

Our work takes place in individual sessions and everyday classroom experiences. We plan carefully, record observations and review how children are using their skills beyond a particular activity. We ask not only what a child is learning, but whether our support is making daily experiences more accessible, meaningful and manageable.

In our books, inclusion is much more than being present in the same space as other children. It is belongingness built through connection with people, children and environment, participation built through planning, discussion and education of the teachers about neurodiversity, skilling up the adults, teachers in the environment rather than placing the entire onus of inclusion on the children or therapists. 

Our sessions are entirely transparent giving visibility to the parents about how we go about things, we have periodical reviews with parents to understand how the goals in therapy are getting transferred to the environment, to facilitate that transfer of learning, and also to understand the meaningfulness of goals in the child’s context. 

# How We Put This into Practice

We hold clear goals for our work, while remaining willing to question our assumptions and change our approach when a child’s experience tells us we need to. 
In practice, this means . We work closely with and regularly review . When something is not helping a child, we see that as a feedback to our practice and make changes until what we do becomes engaging and meaningful for the child. 

Our periodical reviews with parents help us understand the child’s needs in other environments better and organise our goals accordingly. We see this as a shared goal between us and the family.
As a team, we sit every week to evaluate our goals, interventions and the child’s learning and ensure this informs our everyday practice to make sure that the time the child spends at Sambhavam is efficient and effective in supporting them achieve meaningful milestones and explore new areas. This is our team work and we believe everyone brings their best to the table in terms of their observations, insights backed by data points.
